cover.subtitle: Zomato/Swiggy Case Study
cover.tagline: Customer, restaurant and rider apps plus an ops dashboard: 10 subsystems designed end to end

items: Customer: ==browse and search== restaurants, build a cart
Customer: **place and pay**, track the order live, rate
Restaurant: accept orders and update their status
Rider: accept deliveries offered by dispatch

rows: no double charge, no lost order

blocks.text: 3. Order load: from day to peak

items: ~100 browse sessions per order gives ~==30K search/menu QPS== at peak
So the **read path** scales independently of the write path

blocks.title: INTERVIEW TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: Size for the ==500/s== dinner peak and ~30K read QPS, not the 58/s average. Orders are ~9 TB/year, but the 50 GB menu set fits in cache.

rows.label: Core:
rows.text: catalog, cart, order, pay, dispatch, tracking, notify, pricing

blocks.title: INTERVIEW TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: Sync only order and pay; rest on Kafka.

items: Find restaurants and dishes ==near a location==
Filter by cuisine, rating and ETA, then **rank**
A geohash or H3 cell narrows the radius first
Then filter on open now and on cuisine
Ranker scores relevance, ETA, rating and conversion
App sends lat/lng and query to the gateway
Search asks ES for ~500 nearby candidates
Cached menu snippets are attached and returned
Stale index shows closed restaurants: ==rebuild from CDC stream==
ES down: serve cached top-N per H3 cell

blocks.title: INTERVIEW TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: ES gives a fast, slightly stale shortlist. Redis and checkout hold the truth.

items: Be the ==source of truth== for an order's lifecycle
Emit one event on every transition
Callbacks: restaurant accept, ready; rider pick up
Outbox relay publishes each event to Kafka
No accept in **3 min**: timeout job auto-cancels, refunds
Duplicate request returns the stored result
Track order success rate and accept latency
Alert on orders non-terminal for > 1 hour

blocks.title: TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: Only the order service moves status, one versioned transition at a time, and every move is an event.

items: Disposable: a lost cart costs one re-add

blocks.note: ids and qty only, no prices

items: Price/stock change: return a ==diff== to confirm

blocks.title: INTERVIEW TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: Cart disposable, price not: re-price server-side, lock quote, create order.

items: Lost webhook: poll PSP after ==30 s==
Track success (> 97%), refund time, webhook lag
Fires at PLACED; offer delayed by prep minus travel
Score: pickup ETA, load, acceptance; top gets **20 s**
Batching can merge two nearby orders
One offer **at a time**, never a broadcast
Decline or timeout moves to the ==next rider==
Accept is final once the versioned write lands

blocks.title: TIP:
blocks.text: Delay the offer by prep time minus travel time, so the rider does not wait at the restaurant.

items: No taker: widen radius, ==incentive==, **alert ops** at 5 min
Track assignment time (**< 60 s**), acceptance, idle time, ETA error

blocks.title: INTERVIEW TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: One rider at a time; a versioned write picks the winner.

items: Show the rider's ==live position== on the customer's map
Show an accurate ==ETA==, recomputed as traffic changes
Keep freshness **under 5 s** for 500K active riders
500K riders ÷ 4 s ping = ==125K writes/s==, via stateless ingest
Redis keeps latest position only; Kafka feeds cold history
Gateway subscribes to the order's rider channel and forwards updates
ETA recomputed ~30 s from road graph and traffic

blocks.note: history goes to time-series store or S3

blocks.title: TIP:
blocks.text: The 60 s TTL drops offline riders automatically, so no cleanup job is needed.

items: Socket drops: reconnect with ==backoff==, then poll every 10 s
Stationary rider: **throttle** pings to save battery
Track update lag p99, against the 5 s target
Track ETA error versus actual delivery time

blocks.title: INTERVIEW TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: Keep only the latest ping in Redis, stream it over WebSocket, and fall back to polling.

items: Tell all parties about ==every order event==
Push, SMS, in-app, email; dedupe on `event_id`
Restaurant alerts **retry louder** than customer ones

blocks.title: 6. Failures and Metrics
items: SMS outage: ==secondary provider==; per-user rate limit
Track delivery rate, p99 < 5 s, opt-outs

blocks.title: INTERVIEW TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: Dedupe on event_id, push first, SMS fallback, DLQ: no event lost or sent twice.

items: Degrade: recommendations off first, never checkout
